paragraphs: Assured Guaranty Ltd. (AGL and, together with its subsidiaries, Assured Guaranty or the Company) is a Bermuda-based holding company that provides, through its wholly-owned operating subsidiaries, credit protection products to the U.S. and non-U.S. public finance (including infrastructure) and structured finance markets. Assured Guaranty also participates in the asset management business.

Through its financial guaranty insurance subsidiaries, the Company applies its credit underwriting judgment, risk management skills and capital markets experience primarily to offer financial guaranty insurance, including nonpayment insurance, that protects holders of debt instruments and other monetary obligations from defaults in scheduled payments. If an obligor defaults on a scheduled payment due on an obligation, such as scheduled principal or interest payment (collectively, debt service), the Company is required under its unconditional and irrevocable financial guaranty to pay the shortfall of the scheduled amount to the holder of the obligation, but generally cannot be required by the holder to pay on an accelerated basis. The Company markets its financial guaranty insurance directly to issuers and underwriters of public finance and structured finance securities as well as to investors in such obligations. The Company guarantees obligations issued principally in the U.S. and the United Kingdom (U.K.), and also guarantees obligations issued in other countries and regions, including Western Europe and Australia. The Company also provides specialty insurance and reinsurance on transactions with risk profiles similar to those of its structured finance exposures written in financial guaranty form.

The Company participates in the asset management business through its ownership interest in Sound Point Capital Management, LP (Sound Point, LP) and certain of its investment management affiliates (together with Sound Point, LP, Sound Point), as described in greater detail under Item 1. Business — Asset Management.

On January 21, 2026, the Company purchased all of the outstanding share capital in Warwick Company (UK) Limited (which is the 100% indirect owner of Assured Life Reinsurance Ltd. (Assured Life Re, f/k/a Warwick Re Limited), for a purchase price of $158 million, subject to certain post-closing adjustments (Assured Life Re Acquisition). Assured Life Re is a Class E long-term (life) reinsurance company incorporated and registered in Bermuda and is rated BBB (Outlook Positive) (1/28/26) by Fitch Ratings, Inc. Assured Life Re focuses on annuity reinsurance including U.K. bulk purchase annuity (pension risk transfers) and U.S. multi-year guaranteed annuity transactions. The Assured Life Re Acquisition represents the Company's first platform dedicated solely to the life and annuity reinsurance business, further diversifying the risk profile and revenue opportunities of the Company.

See Item 1A. Risk Factors — Strategic Risks, captioned "The Assured Life Re Acquisition may negatively impact the Company, including how it is perceived by its investors, regulators, rating agencies or obligors it insures, as well as Assured Life Re's business relationships," "Entering the life and annuity reinsurance business may present integration risks and other risks specific to the life and annuity reinsurance business that could have a negative effect on the Company's business, results of operations or financial condition," "Strategic transactions may not result in the benefits anticipated" and "The Company makes assumptions when pricing its life and annuity reinsurance products relating to longevity, mortality, policy lapses, withdrawals, surrenders, investment returns and expenses, and significant deviations in experience could negatively affect the Company's financial condition and results of operations."

The Company continually evaluates its key business strategies, which fall into four areas: (i) growth of its insurance and asset management businesses; (ii) loss mitigation, (iii) enhancement of investment returns through alternative investments; and (iv) capital management. The Company seeks to grow its core financial guaranty insurance business through new business production in established sectors and jurisdictions and by entering into new markets, lines and classes of business, and also through acquisitions of financial guarantors that are no longer actively writing new business (legacy financial guarantors) or their insured portfolios through reinsurance or novations. In addition, the Company seeks to leverage its core credit competencies by expanding its business into revenue streams independent of its financial guaranty insurance business, such as annuity reinsurance through its life and annuity reinsurance platform and its asset management business, with the objective of diversifying net income growth and generating high-return business opportunities. The Company also employs a number of strategies in an effort to mitigate losses in its insured portfolio. The Company seeks to optimize its investment returns and expects its relationship with Sound Point to enhance alternative investment opportunities for its insurance subsidiaries. Finally, the Company pursues strategies to efficiently allocate and utilize capital within the Assured Guaranty group.

Financial guaranty insurance generally provides an unconditional and irrevocable guaranty that protects the holder of a debt instrument or other monetary obligation against non-payment of debt service when due. Upon an obligor's default on scheduled payments due on the debt obligation, whether due to its insolvency or otherwise, the Company is generally required under the financial guaranty contract to pay the investor the principal and interest shortfalls when due.

Financial guaranty insurance may be issued to all of the investors of the guaranteed series or tranche of a municipal bond or structured finance loan or other debt obligation at the time of issuance or it may be issued to specific individual holders of such obligations who purchase the Company's credit protection either in the secondary market or on a bilateral basis where the borrower has purchased the financial guaranty to benefit its own obligations.

Both issuers of, and investors in, financial instruments may benefit from financial guaranty insurance. Issuers benefit when they purchase financial guaranty insurance for their new issue debt transaction because the insurance may have the effect of lowering an issuer's interest cost over the life of the debt transaction to the extent that the insurance premium charged by the Company is less than the net present value of the difference between the yield on the obligation insured by Assured Guaranty (which carries the credit rating of the specific subsidiary that guarantees the debt obligation) and the yield on the debt obligation if sold on the basis of its uninsured credit rating. The principal benefit to investors is that the Company's financial guaranty provides increased certainty that scheduled payments will be received when due. The Company's financial guaranty of bank loans may also provide policyholders with reduced regulatory capital requirements or relief from internally managed credit limits. Additionally, financial guaranty insurance may improve the marketability and liquidity of obligations, especially obligations with complex structures or backed by asset classes new to the market. In general, and especially in such instances, investors may be able to sell insured bonds more quickly and at a better price than the comparable uninsured debt.

As an alternative to traditional financial guaranty insurance, the Company also may provide credit protection relating to a particular debt obligation or obligor through a credit derivative contract, such as a credit default swap (CDS). Under the terms of a CDS, the provider of credit protection agrees to make a specified payment to the buyer of credit protection if one or more specified credit events occurs with respect to a reference obligation or entity. In general, the Company's CDS provide that failure to pay debt service on the reference obligation is a credit event, but the Company's rights and remedies under a CDS may be different and more limited than under financial guaranty insurance.

The Company also offers credit protection through reinsurance, and in the past has provided reinsurance to other financial guaranty insurers with respect to their financial guaranties of public finance, infrastructure and structured finance obligations. The Company believes that the financial guaranty opportunities currently available to it in the reinsurance market primarily consist of potentially assuming portfolios of transactions from legacy financial guarantors.

General Obligation Bonds are full faith and credit obligations that are issued by states, their political subdivisions and other municipal issuers, and are supported by the general obligation of the issuer to pay from available funds and by a pledge of the issuer to levy property taxes in an amount sufficient to provide for the full payment of the bonds.

Tax-Backed Bonds are obligations that are supported by the issuer from specific and discrete sources of taxation and tax-backed revenue bonds. Tax-backed obligations may be secured by a lien on specific pledged tax revenues, such as a gasoline or excise tax, or an income tax, or incrementally from growth in property tax revenue associated with growth in property values. These obligations also include obligations secured by special assessments levied against property owners and often benefit from issuer covenants to enforce collections of such assessments and to foreclose on delinquent properties. Lease revenue bonds typically are general fund obligations of a municipality or other governmental authority that are subject to annual appropriation or abatement; projects financed and subject to such lease payments ordinarily include real estate or equipment serving an essential public purpose.

Municipal Utility Bonds are obligations of all forms of municipal utilities, including electric, water and sewer utilities and resource recovery revenue bonds. These utilities may be organized in various forms, including municipal enterprise systems, authorities or joint action agencies.

The risks and uncertainties discussed below are not the only ones the Company faces. However, these are the risks that the Company's management believes are material. The Company may face additional risks or uncertainties that are not presently known to the Company or that management currently deems immaterial, and such risks or uncertainties also may impair its business or results of operations. The risks discussed below could result in a significant or material adverse effect on the Company's financial condition, results of operations, capital, liquidity, business prospects and/or share price.

The following summarizes some of the risks and uncertainties that may adversely affect the Company's financial condition, results of operations, capital, liquidity, business prospects and/or share price. It is provided for convenience and should be read together with the more expansive explanations below this summary.
•Developments in the global financial markets, political systems and economy generally.
•Significant budget deficits and pension funding and revenue shortfalls of certain public finance obligors that issue obligations the Company insures.
•Significant risks from large individual or correlated exposures.
•Losses on obligations insured by the Company significantly in excess of those expected by the Company or recoveries significantly below those expected by the Company.

On April 2, 2025, the U.S. administration announced a "reciprocal tariff" strategy under the authority of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) entailing extensive global tariff increases, with the objective of rectifying trade practices that contribute to large and persistent annual U.S. goods trade deficits. The announcement of global tariffs disrupted international trade, sent shocks through the global economy, and heightened volatility in the financial markets. The U.S. subsequently postponed newly announced reciprocal tariffs, which took effect on August 7, 2025. On August 29, 2025, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit ruled that the U.S. administration had exceeded its authority under the IEEPA but permitted the tariffs to remain in effect to provide time for the government to appeal. The U.S. Supreme Court granted certiorari on September 9, 2025, and heard oral arguments on the case on November 5, 2025; on February 20, 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court held that the IEEPA does not authorize the President of the United States to impose tariffs. The U.S. administration has indicated that tariffs found to be illegal by the U.S. Supreme Court will be replaced with alternative import taxes as uncertainty remains. U.S. tariffs can add to inflation, and the Company believes that ongoing uncertainty may increase volatility in U.S. equities and other risk assets, curb corporate capital and consumer spending and raise the risk of recession. Market volatility and the risk of recession may impact the Company in different ways. The Company believes that a recession may make it more likely that obligors whose obligations it guarantees will default. However, market volatility may also cause credit spreads to widen as investors seek security, which tends to create new business opportunities for the Company.

paragraphs: Assured Guaranty Ltd. (AGL and, together with its subsidiaries, Assured Guaranty or the Company) 為一家設立於百慕達的控股公司，透過其百分之百擁有之營運子公司，提供信用保護產品給美國與非美國之公共財務（包括基礎建設）及結構性財務市場。Assured Guaranty 亦參與資產管理業務。

透過其財務擔保保險子公司，該公司運用其信用承保判斷、風險管理技能及資本市場經驗，主要提供財務擔保保險，包括非支付保險，以保護債務工具及其他金錢義務之持有人免於預期支付之違約。若義務人未按期支付應償還之本金或利息（合稱為債務服務），該公司依其無條件且不可撤銷之財務擔保，需支付應償還金額之差額給義務之持有人，但一般情況下，持有人無法要求該公司加速支付。該公司直接向公共財務及結構性財務證券之發行者與發行者經銷商以及該義務之投資者行銷其財務擔保保險。該公司擔保之義務主要發行於美國與英國（U.K.），並也擔保發行於其他國家與地區之義務，包括西歐與澳洲。該公司亦提供專門保險與再保險服務，針對風險特質與其結構性財務 exposures 類似之交易。
該公司透過其在 Sound Point Capital Management, LP (Sound Point, LP) 及部分投資管理附屬機構之持股權益參與資產管理業務（合稱 Sound Point, LP 及 Sound Point），如 Item 1. Business — Asset Management 所述更詳細說明。

於 2026 年 1 月 21 日，該公司購入 Warwick Company (UK) Limited（為 Assured Life Reinsurance Ltd. (Assured Life Re, f/k/a Warwick Re Limited) 之 100% 間接所有者）所有發行股份，購價為 1.58 億美元，扣除後續關閉調整（Assured Life Re Acquisition）。Assured Life Re 為一 Class E 長期（壽險）再保險公司，設立並註冊於百慕達，並由 Fitch Ratings, Inc. 給予 BBB（展望正面）（1/28/26）評級。Assured Life Re 關注年金再保險業務，包括英國批量購買年金（退休金風險轉移）與美國多年期保證年金交易。Assured Life Re Acquisition 表示該公司首個專門從事壽險與年金再保險業務之平台，進一步分散該公司之風險特質與收入機會。

請參閱 Item 1A. Risk Factors — Strategic Risks，標題為 "The Assured Life Re Acquisition may negatively impact the Company, including how it is perceived by its investors, regulators, rating agencies or obligors it insures, as well as Assured Life Re's business relationships," "Entering the life and annuity reinsurance business may present integration risks and other risks specific to the life and annuity reinsurance business that could have a negative effect on the Company's business, results of operations or financial condition," "Strategic transactions may not result in the benefits anticipated" 和 "The Company makes assumptions when pricing its life and annuity reinsurance products relating to longevity, mortality, policy lapses, withdrawals, surrenders, investment returns and expenses, and significant deviations in experience could negatively affect the Company's financial condition and results of operations."

該公司持續評估其關鍵業務策略，歸納為四個領域：(i) 保險與資產管理業務之成長；(ii) 損失緩解；(iii) 透過替代投資提升投資回報；以及 (iv) 資本管理。該公司透過在已建立之產業與司法管轄區產生新業務，以及進入新市場、業務線與類別，並透過收購不再積極承做新業務之財務擔保公司（遺留財務擔保公司）或其被保險組合透過再保險或轉讓契約，來成長其核心財務擔保保險業務。此外，該公司亦透過其壽險與年金再保險平台與資產管理業務，擴展其業務至與財務擔保保險業務無關之收入來源，目標為分散淨收入成長與產生高回報之業務機會。該公司亦運用多種策略以緩解其被保險組合之損失。該公司亦致力於優化其投資回報，並預期其與 Sound Point 之關係可提升其保險子公司之替代投資機會。最後，該公司追求策略以有效配置與運用 Assured Guaranty 羣體之資本。
財務擔保保險通常提供無條件且不可撤銷之擔保，保護債務工具或其他金錢義務之持有人免於應償還金額之違約。若義務人未按期支付債務義務之應償還本金或利息（無論因破產或其他原因），該公司依財務擔保契約一般需支付投資者應償還金額之差額。
財務擔保保險可能發行給所有擔保系列或交易之投資者，或可能發行給特定個別持有人，這些持有人在發行時購買該公司之信用保護，或在二級市場或雙邊基礎上購買財務擔保以受益其自身義務。

發行者與投資者皆可能從財務擔保保險中受益。發行者在發行新債券時購買財務擔保保險，可降低其利息成本，前提是保險費率低於擔保公司所收取的淨現值差額，該差額為擔保債券的收益率與未擔保債券的收益率之間的差額。投資者的主要受益在於本公司提供的財務擔保可增加定期付款按時收到的確定性。本公司對銀行貸款的財務擔保亦可能為保單持有人提供降低監管資本要求或免除內部管理信用額度的優勢。此外，財務擔保保險可能提高義務的市場流通性與流動性，特別是結構複雜或由市場新興資產類別擔保的義務。總體而言，尤其在這些情況下，投資者可能能更快出售擔保債券，並以較佳價格出售與未擔保債務相對應的債券。
作為傳統財務擔保保險的替代方案，本公司亦可能透過信用衍生合約提供特定債務義務或義務人的信用保護，例如信用違約交換（CDS）。根據CDS條款，信用保護提供者同意在特定信用事件發生時，向信用保護買方支付指定金額。一般而言，本公司CDS的條款規定未能支付債務利息為信用事件，但本公司在CDS下的權利與救濟措施可能與財務擔保保險不同且較有限。
本公司亦透過再保險提供信用保護，過去已為其他財務擔保保險公司提供再保險，針對其對公共財務、基礎建設及結構性財務義務的擔保。本公司認為目前在再保險市場中，可供其使用的財務擔保機會主要為潛在地承接來自傳統財務擔保機構的交易組合。
一般義務債券為全額信用義務，由州政府、其政治子單位及其他市政發行者發行，並由發行者從可用資金中支付及透過發行者對徵收財產稅的承諾來支持，以確保足夠的資金用以償還債券。
稅務擔保債券為由發行者從特定且明確的稅收來源及稅務擔保收入債券所支持的義務。稅務擔保義務可能由特定徵收的稅收收入擔保，例如汽油稅或消費稅，或所得稅，或因財產價值增長而產生的財產稅收入增量。這些義務亦包括由對財產所有者徵收的特別評估所擔保的義務，並常受益於發行者承諾執行這些評估的收款及對拖欠財產進行拍賣的契約。
市政公用事業債券為所有形式的市政公用事業義務，包括電力、水與下水道公用事業及資源回收收入債券。這些公用事業可能以不同形式設立，包括市政企業系統、機構或共同行動機構。

paragraphs: 為更詳細說明事件、趨勢與不確定性，以及資本、流動性、信用、營運與市場風險，以及影響本公司的關鍵會計政策與會計估計，請完整閱讀以下對本公司財務狀況與營運結果的討論與分析，並與本公司合併財務報表及其附註說明一併參考，這些內容載於本Form 10-K的其他部分。以下對本公司財務狀況與營運結果的討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。請參閱「前瞻性陳述」以取得更多資訊。本公司的實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因可能是多種因素，包括下文及本Form 10-K其他部分所討論的那些因素，特別是「風險因素」與「前瞻性陳述」部分。
本Form 10-K中已省略與本公司營運結果比較2024年與2023年結果相關的討論。本公司2024年與2023年結果的比較內容，請參閱本公司於2024年12月31日財務年度所發布的年度報告Form 10-K，於第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果的討論與分析」中。
本公司將營運結果分為兩個獨立的應報告分部，保險與資產管理，這與本公司主要營運決策者審視業務以評估表現與分配資源的方式一致。本公司企業本部與其他活動（包括財務擔保VIEs（FG VIEs）與CIVs）則分開列示。
在保險分部，本公司向美國與非美國的公共財務（包括基礎建設）與結構性財務市場提供信用保護產品。本公司透過對Sound Point的股權參與資產管理業務。請參閱第一部分，第1項「業務」－資產管理，以及第8項「財務報表與補充資料」，附註1「業務與會計基礎」。
企業本部主要由發行公開股權或債務的控股公司的營運結果組成。其他類別主要包含合併FG VIEs與CIVs（FG VIE與CIV合併）的影響。請參閱第8項「財務報表與補充資料」，附註2「分部資訊」。

2025 年 4 月 2 日，美國政府宣佈根據國際緊急經濟權力法案（IEEPA）推行一項 "相互關稅" 策略，包含廣泛的全球關稅提高，目標為修正導致美國年度商品貿易逆差持續且巨大的貿易做法。全球關稅的宣佈幹擾了國際貿易，對全球經濟造成衝擊，並提高財務市場的波動性。美國隨後延後新宣佈的相互關稅，原定於 2025 年 8 月 7 日生效。2025 年 8 月 29 日，美國聯邦ircuit上訴法院裁定美國政府根據 IEEPA 擅自擴權，但允許關稅繼續生效，以提供時間讓政府提出上訴。2025 年 9 月 9 日，美國最高法院受理上訴，並於 2025 年 11 月 5 日聆聽該案口頭辯論；2026 年 2 月 20 日，美國最高法院裁定 IEEPA 不允許美國總統課徵關稅。美國政府表示，美國最高法院裁定為非法的關稅將會以替代性進口稅取代，因不確定性仍存。美國關稅可能增加通貨膨脹，本公司認為持續的不確定性可能提高美國股市及其他風險資產的波動性，抑制企業資本與消費者支出，並提高經濟衰退的風險。市場波動與經濟衰退風險可能以不同方式影響本公司。本公司認為經濟衰退可能使本公司擔保之債務人更可能違約。然而，市場波動也可能導致信用 spreads 放寬，因投資者尋求安全，這通常會為本公司創造新的業務機會。

paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列資訊，並與AGL其他提交至美國證券交易委員會（SEC）的申報文件內容一併參考。下列討論的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。然而，這些是本公司管理階層認為具有重大影響的風險。本公司可能面臨其他尚未為本公司所知或管理階層目前認為不具重大影響的風險或不確定性，這些風險或不確定性也可能影響其業務或營運結果。下列討論的風險可能會對本公司的財務狀況、營運結果、資本、流動性、業務前景及/或股價造成重大或具體的不利影響。
